The safety and prosperity of such, as they and theirs shall be under the continual protection of God, <reference osisRef="Psa.121.3-Psa.121.8">Psa 121:3-8</reference>. <div eID="gen23000" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23001" type="x-p"/> This appears to be a prayer of the Jews in their captivity, who are solicitous for their restoration. It is in the form of a dialogue. <reference osisRef="Psa.121.1">Psa 121:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Psa.121.2">Psa 121:2</reference>. The person who worships God speaks the two first verses, "I will lift up mine eyes-my help cometh," - <reference osisRef="Psa.121.1">Psa 121:1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Psa.121.2">Psa 121:2</reference>. <reference osisRef="Psa.121.3">Psa 121:3</reference>. The ministering priest answers him, "He will not suffer thy foot to be moved." "He that keepeth thee will not slumber," <reference osisRef="Psa.121.3">Psa 121:3</reference>. <div eID="gen23001" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23002" type="x-p"/> To which the worshipper answers, that he knows that "he who keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep," <reference osisRef="Psa.121.4">Psa 121:4</reference>; but he seems to express a doubt whether he shall be an object of the Divine attention. <reference osisRef="Psa.121.5">Psa 121:5</reference> etc. The priest resumes; and, to the conclusion of the Psalm, gives him the most positive assurances of God's favor and protection. <div eID="gen23002" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23003" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen23003" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23004" type="x-p"/> Unto the hills - Jerusalem was built upon a mountain; and Judea was a mountainous country; and the Jews, in their several dispersions, turned towards Jerusalem when they offered up their prayers to God.
entries.content_plain: Introduction The resolution of a godly man, Psa 121:1 , Psa 121:2 . The safety and prosperity of such, as they and theirs shall be under the continual protection of God, Psa 121:3-8 . This appears to be a prayer of the Jews in their captivity, who are solicitous for their restoration. It is in the form of a dialogue. Psa 121:1 , Psa 121:2 . The person who worships God speaks the two first verses, "I will lift up mine eyes-my help cometh," - Psa 121:1 , Psa 121:2 . Psa 121:3 . The ministering priest answers him, "He will not suffer thy foot to be moved." "He that keepeth thee will not slumber," Psa 121:3 . To which the worshipper answers, that he knows that "he who keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep," Psa 121:4 ; but he seems to express a doubt whether he shall be an object of the Divine attention. Psa 121:5 etc. The priest resumes; and, to the conclusion of the Psalm, gives him the most positive assurances of God's favor and protection. Verse 1 Unto the hills - Jerusalem was built upon a mountain; and Judea was a mountainous country; and the Jews, in their several dispersions, turned towards Jerusalem when they offered up their prayers to God.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen23005" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23006" type="x-p"/> He will not suffer thy foot to be moved - The foundation, God's infinite power and goodness, on which thou standest, cannot be moved; and whilst thou standest on this basis, thy foot cannot be moved.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen23006" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23007" type="x-p"/> He that keepeth Israel - The Divine Being represents himself as a watchman, who takes care of the city and its inhabitants during the night-watches; and who is never overtaken with slumbering or sleepiness. There is a thought in the Antigone of Sophocles, that seems the counterpart of this of the psalmist, Ταν σαν, Ζευ, δυναμιν τις ανδρων Ὑπερβασια κατασχοι, Ταν ουθ' ὑπνος αἱ - ρει ποθ' ὁ παντογηρως, Ακαματοι τε θεων Μηνες; <div eID="gen23007" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23008" type="x-p"/> Antig. ver. 613, Edit. Johnson. <div eID="gen23008" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23009" type="x-p"/> Shall men below control great Jove above,Whose eyes by all-subduing sleep <div eID="gen23009" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23010" type="x-p"/> Are never closed, as feeble mortals' are;But still their watchful vigil keep <div eID="gen23010" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23011" type="x-p"/> Through the long circle of th' eternal year? <div eID="gen23011" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23012" type="x-p"/> Franklin.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen23012" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23013" type="x-p"/> The sun shall not smite thee by day - Thus expressed by the Chaldee: "The morning spectres shall not smite thee by day, during the government of the sun; nor the nocturnal spectres by night, during the government of the moon." I believe the psalmist simply means, they shall not be injured by heat nor cold; by a sun-stroke by day, nor a frost-bite by night.
